notes: Batch H (SGLT2 inhibitors, SGLT2/metformin combinations, sulfonylureas, repaglinide). 1) Dapagliflozin/metformin: the clinic lists a '10 mg + 1000 mg' tablet; no such strength is licensed in the UK. UK tablets are 5 mg/850 mg and 5 mg/1,000 mg taken twice daily (10 mg dapagliflozin a day). Data use these UK tablets; this is said in formulations[].note. 2) Gliclazide: the clinic product is a 60 mg modified-release tablet. The UK 60 mg prolonged/modified-release generic SmPCs checked (emc-102252, emc-14497) were used; the originator's 60 mg SmPC is not on emc (only its 30 mg MR, emc-1321, not used). Neither 60 mg SmPC checked states that the tablet can be divided, so no halving advice is given. 3) Glimepiride: the originator product is not on emc; the UK generic SmPCs (emc-10743/10744, last updated 2021) were used. 4) Repaglinide: the originator is not on emc; the UK generic SmPC emc-12974 was used (emc-15021 checked: same 4.3). 5) Empagliflozin: emc product pages 7703 and 5441 serve the same SmPC text; only emc-7703 is cited. 6) Sulfonylurea allergy: the SmPCs contraindicate use with hypersensitivity to other sulfonylureas or sulfonamides; SPS (2026) says cross-reactivity between antibiotic and non-antibiotic sulfonamides is not expected. Both are kept as separate rules (contraindicated per SmPC; info per SPS). 7) Breastfeeding: every SmPC in this batch says do not use (gliclazide: contraindicated in 4.3). SPS says there is limited or no information for antidiabetics other than insulin and metformin; it does not clear these medicines. 8) Repaglinide + trimethoprim 'should be avoided' (SmPC 4.5). Co-trimoxazole contains trimethoprim, but the SmPC names only trimethoprim, so no co-trimoxazole rule was made; the integrator may wish to review. 9) New groups: biguanide (metformin-containing medicines; sitagliptin/metformin and vildagliptin/metformin from batch I are NOT added here because their SmPCs were not read), insulin-secretagogue. Members for group:insulin, dpp4-inhibitor, glp1-agonist, beta-blocker, thiazide, loop-diuretic, ace-inhibitor, arb, corticosteroid, beta2-agonist, sympathomimetic, fibrate, tetracycline, salicylate, progestogen, laxative, thyroid-hormone are expected from other batches. 10) BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). 11) Lithium, gemfibrozil, ciclosporin, deferasirox, rifampicin, phenylbutazone, danazol, chlorpromazine, cimetidine and colesevelam interactions are recorded in the interactions sections only: they are not in the master list. 12) Conflict between UK SmPCs on heart failure: the dapagliflozin/metformin SmPC (emc-7612, 4.3) contraindicates acute or chronic disease that may cause tissue hypoxia including cardiac failure, with no allowance for stable heart failure; the empagliflozin/metformin SmPC (emc-11421) and the metformin SmPC allow stable chronic heart failure with monitoring and contraindicate only acute/unstable/decompensated heart failure. Each medicine follows its own SmPC. 13) Dapagliflozin/metformin SmPC 4.5 does not include the lithium or OCT2-inhibitor (trimethoprim) statements that appear in the dapagliflozin and empagliflozin/metformin SmPCs; no such rules were made for it. 14) Glimepiride SmPC 4.5 gives no action for most listed interactions, so those rules are level info (effect tags kept). 15) Quotes were checked with lib/text.mjs quoteFound (the same function as fetchtext --check): 928 quotes, 0 not found. 16) AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker, log scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/H-I.md): all 13 batch H SmPCs re-read (4.1-4.6). Fixes: gliclazide/glimepiride miconazole rules limited to the miconazole oral gel formulation (otherFormulations); gliclazide and glimepiride added to group non-antibiotic-sulfonamide (SPS: all sulfonylureas have a sulfonamide group) and their SmPC sulfonamide-allergy contraindications now also list that group, with a separate SPS info rule for thiazide/loop-diuretic allergy (no cross-reactivity expected between non-antibiotic classes); empagliflozin renal dose rule now covers every eGFR < 60 (no lower bound); new rules for pancreatitis (batch O condition id), restricted food intake (malnutrition), metabolic-acidosis and acute-alcoholism (metformin combinations, 4.3), inhaled corticosteroids (metformin combinations: SmPC says glucocorticoids by local routes), gliclazide hypoglycaemia-prone and cutaneous corticosteroids (SmPC names cutaneous preparations; the engine ignores group matches for skin products, so one rule per skin product), glimepiride hypoglycaemia risk factors (info), repaglinide alcohol (info); repaglinide carbamazepine/St John's wort raised from monitor to caution (4.4 "used with caution or be avoided"). Note 8 superseded: the repaglinide trimethoprim rule already fires for co-trimoxazole because rule.other matches by ingredient (checked with a scratch build).
